messages:
maria (ML): quick note — during the v2 int8 bring-up I saw a ~3.2pt drop in NDCG@10 on our prod_holdout after we started splitting docs into labeled passages. MRR stayed ~flat. anyone seen this pattern?

tuan (Rerank): hmm, labeled passages? like we add 'Passage 1:' text? that could be a strong signal change. can you paste the eval cmd and a couple examples?

maria (ML): eval: `./eval_rerank --model=rnk-v2-int8 --cohort=prod_holdout --format=passage_split --k=10 --seed=42`
example before: `how to factory reset my router` (single-line)
example after splitter: `Context:
Passage 1: how to factory reset my router` (split + small heading inserted)

kevin (Infra): we rolled html_cleaner and whitespace collapse yesterday. that reduces tokens and may shift priming. did token counts change?

maria (ML): tokens/doc mean 124 -> 118 after change. NDCG@10 drop -0.031, MRR -0.002. tails (rank 5-10) took most of the hit.

frances (Data): the splitter started injecting short labels to help downstream. didn't expect reranker fragility. maybe the model learned to heavily weight those tokens.

maria (ML): confirmed splitter inserts 'Context:' and 'Passage X:' — small but consistent.

tuan (Rerank): plan: run 3-way ablation: (A) passage_split with labels, (B) passage_split stripped of labels, (C) whole_doc. compare NDCG/MRR and token distributions. i'll take A/B token diffs.

sam (Ops): i'll handle candidate-pool diffs and run a 2k smoke. kicking off job.

ci-bot: job rerank-smoke-1715009999 started by sam — https://ci.internal/jobs/1715009999

maria (ML): also check PTQ config — are we doing per-channel quant? different quant clipping plus small input drift could amplify. cfg snippet: `mode: perchannel, clip: mse, calib_samples:512`

sam (Ops): candidate diff done, no significant topk identity changes. ordering tiny jitter. posting diff link: https://internal.storage/diffs/1715009999.txt

ci-bot: job rerank-smoke-1715009999 finished — results uploaded to artifacts.

maria (ML): ablation summary from smoke: A (labels): NDCG@10 -3.1pt, B (no labels): -0.4pt, C (whole_doc): -0.2pt. labels correlate strongly with the drop.

frances (Data): wild that a 2-token label can move the metric that much. suggests reranker overfits separators. we should avoid free-text markers; use metadata tags that the reranker ignores or a non-linguistic separator token.

kevin (Infra): immediate mitigation: revert label insertion for the v2 bringup, add preprocessing lint to block arbitrary free-text prefixes, and add a regression gate in CI that runs 1k golden queries and fails deploy on NDCG@10 drop >1.5pt.

tuan (Rerank): i'll add a lightweight token-distribution check to the eval CI: compare mean/std and top-50 token overlap between baseline and candidate. block if significant drift.

maria (ML): opened PR to revert labels + tests + 1k golden gate. also storing raw pre-split inputs in artifact store for later root cause. gdrive: https://gdrive.redwood/reports/1715009999

sam (Ops): will re-run int8 bringup after revert and report numbers in the 11:30 standup. :thumbsup:

maria (ML): thanks all. lesson: tiny textual scaffolding can break reranker evals. keep preprocessors conservative for ranking inputs.
